text:
B: Hello there. Colin, down in Worthing. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah. Lorraine. Wednesbury.
B: Black Country. I had a mate from Dudley years ago, a plasterer. Lovely bloke, couldn't understand a word he said.
A: Well, we're not all like that.
B: No, he was quite extreme. Saw your dog in the picture, I think. Just the top of her head.
A: Bella. She's here now. She's twelve, she's going a bit grey round the face.
B: Ah, bless her. We lost ours, ooh, three years back. I'd have another tomorrow but Maureen's not keen, so I just sort of make a fuss of everyone else's.
A: She's hard work. Canal every morning, rain or not. She don't care.
B: That's the best thing about them, though, isn't it, they get you out. I do the Downs, or the seafront. What do you do when you're not walking her? Working?
A: Not at the minute. I was a machinist, upholstery, till the firm shut. I've said this already once today, I feel like a record.
B: Ha, I know, I was a joiner, I've said that twice. Funny, I used to work with upholsterers. I'd build a window seat and then the upholstery lady'd come and do the cushions, and she'd tell me off if my measurements were out.
A: Well, they would be, wouldn't they. That's what we was always saying. The frames come in wrong and we've got to make it fit.
B: Guilty. I was probably the one sending them in wrong.
A: Probably.
B: Do you still sew at all?
A: Bits. Alterations, for family. The lad I just spoke to said I should do it proper, charge people. They all say that.
B: Well, he's not wrong, but I'll be honest with you, the sewing's the easy bit for you, I should think. It's the rest of it. I was self-employed forty-odd years and my invoices were a shoebox job. Maureen did all my books. I'd have gone under without her and I don't think I ever told her that properly.
A: That's it, though. The forms and that. Gary can't do his own tax disc, never mind.
B: Find yourself a Maureen. Or a library, they do little business sessions sometimes. Mine did.
A: Mm. Maybe. ...It's just you put money in and it all goes wrong, and then where are you. With everything the price it is.
B: No, I know. That's a fair worry. You start small, though, don't you. Word of mouth. I never advertised once.
A: Did you not?
B: Never. People just told people. Anyway, I've gone on. What did you have for dinner last night, go on, something nice.
A: Tea. Shepherd's pie.
B: Tea, sorry, there you go. Lovely.
A: That other lad called a roll a barm. I told him it's a bap.
B: Down here it's just a roll, I'm afraid. Boring lot, we are.
A: Roll's alright. Barm's daft.
B: I'll not tell him you said that. Do you make yours with lamb or is it —
